lead: Climate Week 2026 highlights the intersection of technology and environmental activism, focusing on the impact of AI and data centers on climate change.

stories.title: The Data Center Backlash Should Also Be a Climate Reckoning. It Isn’t Yet
stories.summary: As climate activists increasingly target data centers for their environmental impact, the movement raises questions about public awareness and concern. Despite the pushback against these facilities, the broader implications for climate change remain under-discussed. This article delves into the tension between technological advancement and environmental sustainability.

stories.title: ‘Eat the rich, save the planet’: climate protesters call out big tech’s disconnect from reality
stories.summary: During Climate Week, activists protested outside the offices of major tech companies like OpenAI, Google, and Amazon, criticizing their roles in climate change. The protests highlighted a growing frustration with the perceived disconnect between tech advancements and environmental responsibility. This movement underscores the urgent call for accountability from the tech sector in addressing climate issues.

stories.title: AI is dominating the conversation at Climate Week
stories.summary: As world leaders gather for Climate Week alongside the UN General Assembly, discussions are heavily centered on the role of artificial intelligence in combating climate change. The intersection of AI technology and environmental policy is becoming increasingly prominent, with stakeholders exploring how AI can be leveraged for sustainability efforts.

stories.title: The GPU revolution: Redefining the architecture of innovation
stories.summary: The shift from CPU-centric computing to GPU-accelerated systems has transformed supercomputing capabilities, enabling more efficient climate modeling and simulations. This article discusses how the integration of GPUs into data centers is not only enhancing computational power but also playing a crucial role in addressing complex climate-related problems.

stories.title: The Download: a bid to scrap the virtual wall and AI hits Climate Week
stories.summary: This edition of The Download highlights legislative efforts to dismantle surveillance programs and discusses the prominence of AI at Climate Week. The convergence of technology and environmental policy is becoming a focal point for discussions among lawmakers and activists alike, reflecting a broader trend of integrating AI into climate strategies.

stories.title: The sovereignty imperative: Why AI leaders are taking control of their intelligence
stories.summary: As organizations prioritize AI sovereignty, the implications for climate research and data governance become critical. This article explores how maintaining control over AI systems can enhance the effectiveness of climate initiatives, ensuring that data used in environmental modeling is secure and compliant with local regulations.

stories.title: Climate Week 2026: AI and environmental activism collide
stories.summary: The intersection of AI and climate activism is at the forefront of discussions during Climate Week 2026. With leaders and advocates converging in New York, the focus is on how AI technologies can either exacerbate or mitigate climate challenges. This coverage provides insights into the evolving dialogue around technology's role in environmental sustainability.

stories.title: Climate activists target tech giants over environmental impact
stories.summary: In a series of protests during Climate Week, activists called out tech giants for their environmental impact, particularly in relation to AI and data centers. The movement reflects a growing awareness and urgency to address the climate crisis, challenging the tech industry to take greater responsibility for its ecological footprint.
